sentences.text: These appeals are filed by the insurance company challenging the liability fastened on it to pay compensation, by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, at Shorapur (hereinafter for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.Nos.238/2018 dated 22.04.2019 by the impugned judgment.

02 . The brief facts of the case are that the claimants in the above said MVC cases are either legal representatives of the deceased or the injured, claiming compensation with the contentions that they were traveling in Jeep Reg.No.KA-28-P-1310 (for short 'offended vehicle') from Kembhavi to Hyderabad.

The said Jeep met with an accident near Pulya Nayak Tanda on  -9-  NC: 2024:KHC-K:3754  MFA No. 201801 of 2019  C/W MFA No. 200759 of 2019  MFA No. 200760 of 2019  MFA No. 200761 of 2019  MFA No. 201802 of 2019 12.06.2017 around 06.30 p.m. due to rash and negligent driving of the above said vehicle by its driver.

As a result of which the inmates of the said vehicle had sustained grievous injuries and someone died during the course of The Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197059277/
7 treatment.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the injured - claimants and the legal heirs of the deceased have filed the claim petitions against the owner and the insurer of the offended vehicle for compensation.

03. The appellant - insurer in all above said cases has denied the contents of the claim petitions and contends that the said offended vehicle was a private vehicle and it was used for hire or rewards and carrying the passengers by receiving the fare from the inmates of the vehicle and grossly violated the permit conditions as well as the insurance policy conditions.
Therefore, the appellant - insurer is not liable to pay the compensation and owner of the offended vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
MFA No. 201801 of 2019  C/W MFA No. 200759 of 2019

From the rival contentions of both the parties,
the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues for its determination.
05. The Tribunal has tried the claim petitions separately.
The claimants have lead oral as well as documentary evidence in each MVC cases separately.
The Tribunal could have taken up all these matters together for disposal.

However, they were taken up separately and The Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197059277/
8 disposed of.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 06. The Tribunal after hearing the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record, disposed of the cases and awarded the compensation as referred in the above paras.
The Tribunal held that the said offended vehicle was not taken on hire or reward basis and there is no proof in this regard.
The driver of the said offended vehicle had license to drive the said offended vehicle.
Therefore, the appellant - insurer is liable to pay the compensation.

07 . The appellant - insurance company challenged all these appeals only on the ground that it is not liable to pay the compensation or indemnify the owner of the vehicle, since there was breach of policy conditions as the owner of the vehicle had given the vehicle for hire or reward.
The inmates of the vehicle were paid passengers and their risk is not covered under the policy.

Therefore,
prayed for setting aside the findings of the Tribunal fastening the liability on the insurance company.

08. I have heard the arguments of the learned counsel for both the parties and perused the material The Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197059277/
9 available on records.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 09. The learned counsel for the appellant - insurance company has vehemently contended that in the evidence of PW.1 Smt. Shantabai, she has stated that in the complaint it is mentioned that "the said vehicle was obtained by paying the hire charges".

Even in the FIR /
complaint it is stated that the said vehicle was obtained to  - 12 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:3754  MFA No. 201801 of 2019
C/W MFA No. 200759 of 2019  MFA No. 200760 of 2019  MFA No. 200761 of 2019  MFA No. 201802 of 2019 go to Hyderabad on payment of fare.
These facts clearly indicate that the offended vehicle was taken on hire.
Admittedly, the offended vehicle was private vehicle and it was carrying the passengers for hire or reward, which is not permissible.
It is the violation of condition of permit so also policy conditions.
Hence, the appellant - insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.

10. The learned counsel for the claimants / victims vehemently contended that the contention of the insurer is only on the basis of assumptions and presumptions to avoid its liability to pay the compensation.
None of the document, including the charge-sheet, there is no reference that the persons who were traveling in the said vehicle, were paid passengers.

The owner of the vehicle was examined before the Tribunal and he unequivocally The Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197059277/
10 stated that one of the person, who was traveling in the said vehicle was his relative;

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He obtained the vehicle, by informing him that "they intended to go to Kashi by flight  - 13 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:3754  MFA No. 201801 of 2019  C/W MFA No. 200759 of 2019  MFA No. 200760 of 2019  MFA No. 200761 of 2019  MFA No. 201802 of 2019 from Hyderabad.
Hence, to go to Hyderabad Airport he took the vehicle."

In the cross-examination of most of the witnesses, examined on behalf of the claimants, a suggestions were made by the respondents that "they paid hire charges for taking the vehicle" and the witnesses have denied the same.
 11.
The manager of the insurance company was examined on behalf the insurer, who had admitted that he had no idea, on what basis he had contended that hire charges were paid.
And it was on the basis of presumption as well as the statement made in the FIR (which is not true).
Insurer has been contending that the vehicle was obtained by the inmates, who were traveling in the offended vehicle at the time of accident by paying hire charges to go to Hyedarabad.

The Tribunal has considered the same and on appreciating the evidence in this regard,
held that the there was no iota of evidence to believe that the passengers who were traveling in the said offended

sentences.text: There are no reasons to file appeal by the respondents.

Therefore,
prayed to dismiss the claim petitions.

12. The following question arises for my determination :-
 "Whether owner of offended vehicle had given  the vehicle for hire or reward and hence insurer  is not liable to pay compensation.?"
 13.

As already stated above the fact of the accident and the injuries sustained by the inmates of the offended vehicle and the accident had taken place due to negligence of the driver of the offended vehicle are not seriously disputed.
Therefore, there is no need to go into the said aspect.

It is also worth to note that the insurer has not challenged the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and there is no need to reconsider the same.

Therefore,

15. It appears that one of the inmates had died during the treatment and he had lodged the complaint before the concerned police.
The said complaint is in Telagu language and its Kannada translation is placed on record before the Tribunal.
In the Kannada Translation it was accepted by the Tribunal), there is no reference that inmate had taken the said offended vehicle on hire or reward.
The respondent - insurer did not challenge the correctness of the said Translated version before the Tribunal.
From the cross-examination of Smt. Shantabai it appears that the FIR was confronted to her and question was asked regarding the contents of the said complaint.

It appears that she is an literate witness and going through the said complaint, accepted the contents of  - 16 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:3754  MFA No. 201801 of 2019  C/W MFA No. 200759 of 2019  MFA No. 200760 of 2019  MFA No. 200761 of 2019  MFA No. 201802 of 2019 the said document.

On that basis, the learned counsel for the appellant vehemently contends that PW.1 admitted that she was traveling by paying the hire charges and it is sufficient to interfere in the findings of the Tribunal.

16. The submission of learned counsel for the The Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197059277/
13 appellant is not acceptable.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She is not author of the said document.

She had not given such statement and her statement recorded by the investigating officer was not confronted to her to show that she had stated before the investigating officer that they took offended vehicle by paying hire charges to go to Hyderabad.
Therefore, mere stray sentence stated by her cannot be considered as an admission.
17. The owner of the offended vehicle was examined in this case.
He had given an opportunity to cross-examine him by the insurer.
In the entire cross- examination nothing was brought out to show that he had deposed falsely before the Court.

On the contrary, he has  - 17 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:3754  MFA No. 201801 of 2019  C/W MFA No. 200759 of 2019  MFA No. 200760 of 2019  MFA No. 200761 of 2019  MFA No. 201802 of 2019 stated that one of his relatives obtained the said vehicle to take a drop from Kembhavi to Hyedarabad.
These facts were not denied in the evidence of other witnesses who have sustained injuries.
These facts were not elicited to show that the evidence given by owner of the vehicle was incorrect.

Under these circumstances, the contention of the appellant - insurer that the offended vehicle was taken on hire or reward appears to be only on a guess work of the concerned officer of the insurer, to deny its liability to The Branch Manager vs Smt. Shanta And Ors

18. In the cross-examination of manager of the insurance company, he had stated that the matter was investigated by the investigator appointed by the insurance company.

The said investigator had given detailed report to show that the said offended vehicle was hired by the inmates by paying the charges and traveling in the said offended vehicle against certain conditions.

Admittedly, the said report is not placed on record nor  - 18 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:3754  MFA No. 201801 of 2019  C/W MFA No. 200759 of 2019  MFA No. 200760 of 2019  MFA No. 200761 of 2019  MFA No. 201802 of 2019 investigator has been examined to corroborate the said evidence.
Therefore, the appellant - insurer had suppressed the real fact.
Otherwise there was no reason for the insurer not to place the said materials on record to prove its contention.
Therefore, the Tribunal had taken adverse inference of the same.
There is no reason to interfere in the said findings.
The insurer has utterly failed to prove that said vehicle was taken on hire.
The appeal is devoid of merits.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Therefore, the injured - claimants and the legal heirs of the deceased have filed the claim petitions against the owner and the insurer of the offended vehicle for compensation.
Therefore, the appellant - insurer is not liable to pay the compensation and owner of the offended vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
The Tribunal held that the said offended vehicle was not taken on hire or reward basis and there is no proof in this regard.
The driver of the said offended vehicle had license to drive the said offended vehicle.
Therefore, the appellant - insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
The inmates of the vehicle were paid passengers and their risk is not covered under the policy.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Admittedly, the offended vehicle was private vehicle and it was carrying the passengers for hire or reward, which is not permissible.
It is the violation of condition of permit so also policy conditions.
Hence, the appellant - insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
She had not given such statement and her statement recorded by the investigating officer was not confronted to her to show that she had stated before the investigating officer that they took offended vehicle by paying hire charges to go to Hyderabad.
Therefore, mere stray sentence stated by her cannot be considered as an admission.
He had given an opportunity to cross-examine him by the insurer.
In the entire cross- examination nothing was brought out to show that he had deposed falsely before the Court.
Therefore, the appellant - insurer had suppressed the real fact.
Otherwise there was no reason for the insurer not to place the said materials on record to prove its contention.
Therefore, the Tribunal had taken adverse inference of the same.
There is no reason to interfere in the said findings.
The insurer has utterly failed to prove that said vehicle was taken on hire.
